result_text:
Tickets now carry an assigned support agent, and every ticket list and lookup you named shows it. The full offline test suite passes, and so does the new test. Nothing is committed.

- **Schema** (`schema.sql`): `support_ticket` has a nullable `agent VARCHAR(100)` column. The agent is a free-text name because the repo has no support-agent entity.
- **Model** (`model/SupportTicket.java`): new `agent` component at the end of the record. The old 9-argument constructor remains and leaves the agent null, so existing callers still compile.
- **DataStore**: `createSupportTicket` writes the agent, and all nine ticket queries (`findSupportTicketByNumber`, the open-by-customer/priority/region/sales-rep/product lists, the with-order list, the high-priority-by-region list, and the open-on-date list) select and map it. `updateSupportTicketStatus` only touches status and closed date, so the agent is kept.
- **Service** (`service/SupportTicketService.java`): `create` has a new overload taking an agent. Blank or null becomes unassigned, and a name is trimmed. The old 6-argument `create` delegates with no agent, so the many existing callers are unchanged. `changeStatus` carries the agent over.
- **Test** (`SupportTicketTest.java`): new `agentIsShownAndKeptOnStatusChange`. It covers the agent on lookup and on the customer and priority lists, its survival through in-progress and closed, and an unassigned ticket showing no agent.

I did not add an agent to the demo scenario data, and I did not add the agent to `ClosedTicket` (the closed-tickets report), since it wasn't in your list.
